# Codex task T2: Generate enemy art (ASSETS ONLY — do not edit game.js)

You are the art worker for ASMR MUSOU. Read `ORCHESTRATOR_BRIEF.md` (Japanese) and `CODEX_TASK_ART.md` first for the art direction.
Another Codex worker is editing `game.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, `tests/` at the same time. **Do NOT touch those files.**
You may only create/modify files under `assets/art/` and `assets/ART_LOG.md`.

## What to make

Use your **built-in image generation tool (image_gen)**. Do not call any paid external API. If the built-in tool is unavailable, stop and write the reason in `assets/ART_LOG.md` — do not fake assets with code-drawn images.

Shared style for every image: tactile toy / squishy collectible, soft studio light from upper-left, glossy macro material, bright pastel, simple readable silhouette, tiny cute face (two small dark eyes + small smile) that stays readable at 80 px, centered, full body, generous empty margin, front 3/4 view, **no text, no logos, no ground shadow, no background scenery**. Avoid any existing character likeness.

Generate each as a separate image (square, ≥1024 px source is fine):

| file stem | description |
|---|---|
| `wax_0` | WAX toy intact: round strawberry-pink squishy ball covered by a thin hard glossy candy-wax shell (like a wax-coated sweet). Shell edge visibly thin. |
| `wax_1` | Same character, same pose/size: shell has a web of fine white cracks. |
| `wax_2` | Same character: shell half broken off, big shell flakes missing, soft matte pink squishy interior bulging out through the gaps. |
| `bubble_0` | BUBBLE: mint-green blob built from ~8 plump clear bubble-wrap cells with tiny face on the central cell. |
| `jelly_0` | JELLY: lavender translucent wobbly jelly drop, glossy, slightly squat, tiny face. |
| `ice_0` | ICE: icy-blue faceted ice-candy crystal creature, angular gem silhouette, internal frost, tiny face. |
| `ice_1` | Same ice character with sharp white fracture lines. |
| `boss_0` | BOSS: large golden-peach round squishy wrapped in THICK multi-layer wax shell (visible 2–3 shell layers at the edge like an onion), friendly face. |
| `boss_1` | Same boss with outer shell layer shattered/peeled off in chunks, layer below visible, cracks. |
| `boss_2` | Same boss with all shell gone: glossy soft peach-pink jelly core exposed, slightly bulging, happy face. |

Consistency matters more than detail: same light direction, same face style, same outline thickness across all files. Damage states must keep the same silhouette scale and centering as their intact state so they can be swapped in place in-game.

## Transparency (required)

Final files must be RGBA PNG with real transparent background, saved as `assets/art/<stem>.png`, trimmed to content then padded to a square canvas with ~6% margin, resized to **384×384**, character centered (the circle body center at image center).
- Prefer asking image_gen for a transparent background. If the result is not truly transparent, generate on a flat uniform background color that does not appear in the character (e.g. pure #00FF00 for pink/peach/lavender characters, pure #FF00FF for mint/ice characters) and key it out with Python (`python` = 3.14 with Pillow 12 + numpy available). Do soft edge matting / despill so there is no colored fringe and no leftover rectangle. Translucent jelly may keep partial alpha.
- Write the keying script to `assets/art/tools/key_bg.py` so it is reproducible.
- Keep the raw generated sources in `assets/art/src/` (copy them out of `$CODEX_HOME/generated_images`; do not leave the only copy there).

## Verification (completion criteria)

1. Every file listed above exists in `assets/art/` as 384×384 RGBA PNG; corners are fully transparent (alpha 0) — verify with a Python check and print the results.
2. Make a contact sheet `assets/art/contact_sheet.png` showing all sprites at 384 px and at 80 px over the game's dark navy background (#2a2647) so readability at gameplay scale can be judged. Look at it yourself and regenerate any sprite whose face is unreadable at 80 px, that has a fringe, or that breaks consistency.
3. `assets/ART_LOG.md`: for each file: generation tool name, date (2026-11-22), the exact prompt, number of attempts, adopted/rejected, post-processing, and usage terms as you understand them for images generated by the built-in tool (state uncertainty honestly).

Final message: list of files, what was regenerated and why, any remaining weaknesses.
Do not commit anything to git.
